stories.title: Circle wants the SEC to scrap a Wall Street rule it says hurts stablecoins
stories.summary: Circle has asked the SEC to remove a long-standing Wall Street rule that it says raises costs for stablecoin issuers, according to CryptoSlate. The report does not name the specific rule or detail any SEC response so far.
stories.whyItMatters: A rule change could lower compliance costs for stablecoin issuers and shape how regulators treat dollar-pegged tokens going forward.
whatToWatch: Whether the SEC responds to Circle's request
Any formal rulemaking petition or comment period
questions: Which specific SEC rule is Circle targeting?
How would other stablecoin issuers be affected?

sources.title: Circle wants SEC to erase a costly Wall Street rule holding stablecoins back

stories.title: Ripple's RLUSD stablecoin lands on Coinbase and earns an investment-grade rating from Moody's
stories.summary: Ripple's RLUSD stablecoin became accessible on Coinbase, and Moody's gave it an investment-grade rating, according to CryptoSlate. The two developments give RLUSD both a major exchange listing and a credit-rating endorsement as it seeks wider adoption.
stories.whyItMatters: Exchange access plus a rating from a major credit agency gives RLUSD more legitimacy as it competes with Tether and Circle's USDC.
whatToWatch: Whether other rating agencies follow Moody's
questions: What criteria did Moody's use for the rating?
Does Coinbase access cover all trading pairs or a limited set?

sources.title: Ripple’s RLUSD stablecoin gains Coinbase access as Moody’s awards investment-grade rating

stories.title: Bitcoin developers rush to patch three AI-discovered security flaws
stories.summary: Bitcoin software developers moved quickly to fix three security flaws that an AI tool uncovered, CryptoSlate reported. Separately, CryptoSlate noted that bitcoin options markets priced in a much smaller premium around the recent election than in 2024, and cited a forecast claiming bitcoin could reach $1.6 million by 2036 — though it said 82% of that projection rests on a single assumption.
stories.whyItMatters: Flaws in core Bitcoin software carry network-wide risk, while muted options pricing suggests traders see less event risk now; the long-range price forecast is speculative and worth treating with caution.
whatToWatch: Confirmation that all three flaws are fully patched
Options pricing around future market catalysts
questions: Were the flaws in consensus code or node software?
What single assumption drives most of the $1.6 million forecast?

sources.title: Bitcoin developers rush to fix 3 security flaws after AI uncovers them
Bitcoin options carried a far smaller election premium than in 2024

stories.title: Strategy's STRC preferred shares near $100, a level that could reopen a Bitcoin funding channel
stories.summary: Shares of Strategy's STRC preferred stock are approaching the $100 mark, a level CryptoSlate says could reopen a financing channel the company has used to fund bitcoin purchases. The report ties STRC's price to Strategy's capacity to raise further capital for its bitcoin treasury strategy.
stories.whyItMatters: Strategy is one of the largest corporate holders of bitcoin, so its financing capacity directly affects demand for the asset.
whatToWatch: Any new Strategy bitcoin purchase that follows
questions: What specifically reopens at the $100 threshold — new issuance or a redemption feature?

sources.title: Strategy’s STRC nears $100 level that could reopen a Bitcoin funding channel

stories.title: Only 10% of wallets using the FOMO app on Solana were profitable after fees
stories.summary: A review found that just 10% of wallets using the Solana-based FOMO app ended up profitable once fees were counted, according to CryptoSlate. The finding suggests fees and losses erode returns for most users of the app.
stories.whyItMatters: It is a reminder that retail trading apps and memecoin-style platforms often leave most users worse off, despite hype about quick gains.
whatToWatch: Whether FOMO or similar apps change their fee structure
Any response from the app's operators
questions: How was profitability measured — gross gains or net of all costs?
How does this compare with other Solana trading apps?

sources.title: Only 10% of FOMO app’s Solana wallets were profitable after fees

stories.title: North Korea's $600 million fake-worker scheme has a hidden crypto connection
stories.summary: A report detailed a North Korean scheme that used fake remote IT workers to generate roughly $600 million, and found a crypto connection tied to the operation, according to CryptoSlate. The available report does not fully specify how crypto was used in the scheme.
stories.whyItMatters: Sanctioned state actors using crypto to fund operations remains a key concern for regulators and exchanges working to curb illicit finance.
whatToWatch: Any sanctions or enforcement action tied to the scheme
questions: Which crypto assets or exchanges were involved?
How was the $600 million figure calculated?

sources.title: North Korea’s $600 million fake-worker empire has a hidden crypto connection

stories.title: A divided Fed rate decision threatens Bitcoin's rebound as a December hike looms
stories.summary: The Federal Reserve's latest rate decision reportedly showed division among policymakers, and CryptoSlate says this could threaten bitcoin's recent recovery given the possibility of a December rate hike. The report ties bitcoin's price momentum to the broader interest-rate outlook.
stories.whyItMatters: Interest-rate expectations shape risk appetite across markets, including crypto, so a hawkish shift could pressure bitcoin prices.
whatToWatch: Bitcoin's price reaction to further Fed commentary
questions: How divided was the vote, and which officials dissented?
How likely is a December hike based on current market pricing?

sources.title: Fed’s divided rate decision threatens Bitcoin’s comeback as December hike looms

stories.title: China's tech stock crash wiped out $480 billion while Bitcoin rose 27% over the same stretch
stories.summary: A sharp selloff erased about $480 billion from Chinese tech stocks, while bitcoin gained 27% over the same dates, according to CryptoSlate. The report frames this as a divergence between the two markets rather than proof of a direct cause-and-effect link.
stories.whyItMatters: Divergence between equities and bitcoin feeds the argument that crypto can act as a hedge, though a short overlapping window is not strong evidence of that pattern.
whatToWatch: Whether the divergence holds over a longer period
Capital flows from Chinese investors into crypto markets
questions: Is there evidence of capital rotating from Chinese tech stocks into bitcoin?
How much of bitcoin's gain came from unrelated factors?

sources.title: China’s tech crash erased $480 billion. Bitcoin rose 27% over the same dates
